intro: Procurement analysts rely on Google Sheets for procurement analysts on Mac to reconcile spend and track vendor performance. You spend your day moving between ERP systems and spreadsheets, so speed matters. This guide covers how to handle large data sets and complex formulas without leaving your browser. You will also see how to use Lazur to stay focused while you manage your procurement pipeline.
tldr: Use Google Sheets on Mac via Chrome for the best stability.
Install the web app version to keep your sheets in a separate window.

blocks.text: Setting up your workspace for procurement analysis

Google Sheets runs in your browser. While you can open it in any browser, Chrome offers the best performance on a Mac. You can turn any sheet into a dedicated app. Open your sheet in Chrome. Click the three dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Click Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder. You can now launch your procurement tracker like a native Mac app.
Common procurement analyst tasks in Google Sheets

You likely spend hours cleaning vendor lists or matching purchase orders to invoices. You need to be fast. Use the Tool Finder by pressing Option + /. Type what you need, like freeze or sort. It saves you from digging through menus. If you need to clean data, use the Find and Replace tool with ⌘ + ⇧ + H. This is faster than manual scrolling.

You might hit the 20 million cell limit if you track global spend over many years. Keep your files lean. Use separate tabs for different fiscal years. Do not keep unused formulas in your sheet. They slow down the calculation engine. If you see #REF! or #NAME?, check your range references immediately. These errors often break your entire report.
Memorize these to keep your hands on the keyboard. If you forget one, press ⌘ + / to see the list. It appears as an overlay on your screen. You can search this list for specific actions.

You deal with sensitive contract terms and pricing. Always check your sharing settings. Click the Share button at the top right. Ensure you do not share with anyone outside your organization by mistake. Use the link settings to restrict access to specific people. If you share a view only link, verify the permissions before you send it out.
Working with CSV files from ERP systems

Exporting data from systems like SAP or Oracle often results in CSV files. To import these into your sheet, go to File > Import. Select your file. Choose to replace data or append it. If your data does not align, use the Split text to columns feature. It is under Data > Split text to columns. This is helpful when your ERP exports data in a single column instead of separate fields.

You can automate basic tasks to save time. Use pivot tables to summarize spend by category. Go to Insert > Pivot table. Select your data range. Drag your fields into rows and values. This is better than writing complex countif or sumif formulas that might break when you add new rows.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no official native app. You can create a Progressive Web App shortcut in Chrome to get a dedicated window experience.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts inside your browser.

faq.question: What should I do if my spreadsheet is slow?
faq.answer: Check for broken formulas, remove unused rows or columns, and consider splitting your data into multiple files if you approach the 20 million cell limit.
